relevance_note: One cohort patient carries a TNFAIP3 variant: 'WES revealed a heterozygous c.559C>T (p. Q187X) mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene in patient 7'.
method_note: Read the full Markdown manually; a short Python script only assembled the JSON (no table transcription, because Tables 1-3 and Figures 1-4 are present only as titles, so no per-patient ages, laboratory values such as CRP/ESR, or per-patient drug lists were available). Scope: this is a 7-patient cohort of SLE with lymphoproliferation; only patient 7 carries a TNFAIP3 variant. Patients 1-4 (somatic NRAS), patient 5 (no variant) and patient 6 (PIK3CD, also previously reported as ref. 23) were not given rows because they have no TNFAIP3 variant. Her father (carrier, 'which is from her father') has a row; his clinical status is not reported. Patient 7's grandparents were Sanger-tested negative, but the paper gives neither their number nor which side, so they have no rows; the statement is in both parental_testing_statement cells. Patient 7 features marked 'inferred from group statement' come from statements about all 7 patients (SLE criteria, lymphoproliferation, hepatomegaly/splenomegaly/lymphadenectasis, ANA, IgG, renal 7/7, bone marrow), about 'the other patients' except patient 3 (IgE), or about the 6 'patients with mutations' (6/6 renal, hematologic, recurrent fever; the paper identifies them as patients 1-4, 6 and 7, with no mutation in P5). The checklist item 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' is marked observed from 'hematologic (cytopenia)' involvement; the paper does not call patient 7's cytopenia autoimmune. Skin involvement: 'only 1 patient' of the 6 with mutations, unnamed, so skin lesions stay not reported. is_proband is null for patient 7 because the cohort paper never uses 'proband' or 'index case'. Sex of patient 7 comes from 'her'. Variant class is not named by the authors, so variant_type is not reported. Protein is printed 'p.Q187X' (abstract, results) and 'p. Q187X' (discussion). No functional assay concerns the TNFAIP3 variant (western blot of BIM was done only in the 4 NRAS patients), although the abstract says 'Protein levels were detected in patients with gene mutations by western blot'. The paper says all mutations 'were all found' in ExAC, 1000 Genomes and HGMD; this is not recorded in a field. Contradictions: (1) results list a flare during tapering in patients 1, 3, 4 and 7, but the discussion gives a flare on prednisolone tapering in '3 patients (1, 3, and 4)'; (2) skin involvement in 'only 2 patients' (results, 7 patients) vs 1/6 among carriers (discussion), consistent only if patient 5 counts; (3) the NRAS variant is c.38 A>G p.G13C in the text but c.38G>A p.G13D in the Figure 2 legend (not extracted).
